//: Vercel Hobby permits ONE cron run per day, so this is a daily safety net —
not the real schedule. The engine is designed around a 15-minute tick, and
on a daily-only cadence an attendance confirmation could arrive up to 24
hours after the child was marked present, which is worse than not sending
it. Nothing here is idempotency-sensitive: every stage self-guards, so a
daily run overlapping the 15-minute one is harmless.
The 15-minute tick runs from .github/workflows/cron.yml, which is free and
authenticates with CRON_SECRET. See that file for the GCP migration path.
maxDuration is 60 because Hobby caps Node functions there. Raise it on
Pro or GCP, where a large queue may take longer to drain.
